U01.name: Base Price-Structure Process
U01.purpose: Establish the central price structure: the reference price levels and the rules that govern how every part is priced.
U01.trigger: A new pricing model is stood up, or the annual structure review revises segments and reference levels.
flow: Define the segment and product-line structure the portfolio will be priced against.
Set the reference price levels (list, floor, target, peer) per segment.
Configure the rule logic that maps a part's attributes and cost to a proposed price.
Publish the structure as the governed baseline all downstream steps inherit.
U01.inputs: Product master data, cost data, segment definitions, strategic price positioning.
U01.outputs: A governed price-structure baseline with reference levels and rules per segment.
U01.pain: This is where the central and market levels first diverge. Without one shared structure, every later step compounds the inconsistency.

U02.name: Volume Tiers, Pack & Rounding Rules
U02.purpose: Define quantity-based price tiers, pack sizes, order minimums and the rounding conventions applied to central prices.
U02.trigger: Structure definition, or a change to tier or rounding policy.
flow: Define tier breaks, pack sizes and order minimums per product line.
Define rounding tables bound to segment, currency or channel.
Validate outputs against the reference price levels.
U02.inputs: Reference price levels, tier and pack policy, currency and tax conventions.
U02.outputs: Reusable tier, pack and rounding rules applied automatically during price setting.
U02.pain: Inconsistent tiers and rounding quietly fragment a single price into many slightly different ones across markets.

U03.name: Customer Group Structures
U03.purpose: Link customers into parent and subsidiary structures to support consolidated, group-level pricing.
U03.trigger: A customer group is onboarded or restructured.
flow: Identify the parent and its subsidiary entities.
Define which pricing decisions apply at group versus entity level.
Maintain the grouping as customers change.
U03.inputs: Customer master data, group structure definitions.
U03.outputs: A maintained customer group hierarchy for consolidated pricing.
U03.pain: Without group structures, the same buying group is priced inconsistently across its entities.

U04.name: New-Part Pricing
U04.purpose: Price a brand-new part that has no prior reference point in the system.
U04.trigger: A new part is introduced to the catalogue.
flow: Assign the new part to its family, product line and segment.
Select the pricing method per the segment rule, bridging any missing input.
Generate a proposed first price from cost, rules and any competitive reference.
Simulate margin, then route the proposal for approval and storage.
U04.inputs: New-part master data, cost, segment rule, competitive reference where available.
U04.outputs: An approved first price for the new part.
U04.pain: New parts routinely wait in a manual queue for a first price, delaying availability and leaving revenue uncaptured.

U05.name: Method-Specific Pricing (cost-plus / fixed)
U05.purpose: Apply method-specific pricing (mark-up, cost-plus or fixed price) that overrides the default value or volume method for designated parts or customers.
U05.trigger: A part type or internal customer requires a defined method, for example a fixed mark-up on cost.
flow: Identify the part type or customer and its required method.
Apply the method and ensure it overrides the default methodology.
Validate against corridor and margin floor, then store.
U05.inputs: Part type, cost, method rule, customer flags.
U05.outputs: A method-correct price that overrides the default where required.
U05.pain: Method exceptions tend to bypass the governed rules, creating untracked inconsistencies.

U06.name: Bulk Price Loading
U06.purpose: Load a large set of prices in one operation with validation and a profit-impact preview.
U06.trigger: A mass price load: migration, periodic refresh, or a large new range.
flow: Stage the load file and validate structure and values.
Preview the aggregate margin and revenue impact.
Commit on approval, with the ability to roll back.
Log the load for audit.
U06.outputs: A validated, committed or rolled-back bulk price load.
U06.pain: Without validation and rollback, mass loads are a common source of large, hard-to-trace pricing errors.

U21.name: Margin Model & Value-Based Setting
U21.purpose: Set value-part prices from a margin model: translate internal and external drivers into a target margin, then refine item by item from value attributes.
U21.trigger: Value parts need a value-based price rather than a cost-plus price.
flow: Score internal and external drivers and compute the margin position per product line.
Map the position to a target margin via the calibrated margin model.
Correct the target margin for very high or very low-cost parts.
Set the reference price, then adjust item prices from value attributes, and visualise the margin curve.
U21.inputs: Driver scores, calibration weights, target-margin mapping, value attributes, cost.
U21.outputs: A value-based price per part with a transparent, explainable margin curve.
U21.pain: Without a margin model and a visible curve, value-based pricing is opaque and impossible to defend or scale.

U07.name: Differentiated Increase
U07.purpose: Apply a scoped, differentiated general price change (percentage or absolute) across a chosen set of parts.
U07.trigger: A cost wave, inflation pass-through, or strategic repricing.
flow: Select the scope: families, segments, regions.
Define the differentiated adjustment and any caps.
Simulate the margin and revenue effect.
Route for approval and schedule activation.
U07.inputs: Scope selection, adjustment parameters, cost and margin data.
U07.outputs: An approved, scoped differentiated price adjustment.
U07.pain: A differentiated general increase with reliable impact simulation is one of the most-wanted and least-supported capabilities in practice.

U08.name: Central Pricing & Action Reporting
U08.purpose: Report central price, margin and volume performance to surface where pricing action is needed.
U08.trigger: Periodic review, or an alert on a KPI breach.
flow: Aggregate price, margin and volume by segment and family.
Compare against targets, corridors and prior periods.
Highlight outliers and candidates for action.
U08.outputs: Central pricing performance reports and an action shortlist.
U08.pain: Reporting that does not point to a next action leaves teams reacting late rather than steering.

U22.name: Surcharge, Tariff & Channel Linkage
U22.purpose: Track component surcharges and tariffs and link a cost or price change in one channel to the related service channel.
U22.trigger: A surcharge or tariff change, or a price change in one channel with a dependency in another.
flow: Capture the surcharge or tariff at component level.
Reflect it into the central price build-up.
Propagate the linked change to the related service channel.
Compare the resulting levels against the independent channel.
U22.inputs: Component cost elements, surcharge and tariff schedules, channel linkage, competitive references.
U22.outputs: Central prices that correctly reflect surcharges, tariffs and channel linkage.
U22.pain: Surcharges, tariffs and channel linkage handled off-system are a recurring source of margin error in heavy-parts businesses.

U09.name: Central-to-Market Handover
U09.purpose: Release the approved central price structure to the market organisations in a controlled, transparent way.
U09.trigger: Central prices and structures are approved and ready for local processing.
flow: Package the approved prices, structures and governance parameters.
Release to the market level with a shared status and trail.
Confirm receipt and acceptance before local work begins.
U09.inputs: Approved central prices, corridors, rules, approval limits.
U09.outputs: A confirmed handover of priced structure to the markets.
U09.pain: When central and market levels run on disconnected systems, handover is an opaque manual transfer that loses governance on the way.

U10.name: Market Enablement & Worklist Creation
U10.purpose: Give each market a worklist of exactly what changed and what needs local action.
U10.trigger: A handover or central change that markets must process.
flow: Compute the change each market must act on.
Generate a prioritised local worklist.
Track completion against the worklist.
U10.outputs: A per-market worklist with completion tracking.
U10.pain: Without an automatic worklist, markets discover changes late and process them inconsistently.

U11.name: Market Price Calculation
U11.purpose: Derive the local market list price from the central price using a factor scoring model and local rules.
U11.trigger: A handover, an exchange-rate move, or a scheduled local recalculation.
flow: Compute the market factor against the central price using the local scoring model.
Apply local corridors, caps and rounding.
Check consistency against observed competitive levels.
Simulate local margin and prepare for approval.
U11.inputs: Central price, local scoring criteria, corridors, caps, competitive references.
U11.outputs: A derived, validated market list price.
U11.pain: Manual derivation cannot keep pace with central changes and exchange-rate moves, so local prices drift out of policy.

U12.name: Exchange-Rate Handling
U12.purpose: Manage revisable exchange rates and recalculate affected prices when a rate threshold is crossed.
U12.trigger: An exchange-rate update or a threshold breach.
flow: Maintain the relevant revisable rate set.
Detect when a rate move crosses the recalculation threshold.
Recalculate and flag affected prices for review.
U12.pain: Unmanaged exchange-rate handling either over-reacts to noise or misses material moves entirely.

U13.name: Dealer Price via Discount Structure
U13.purpose: Calculate dealer prices off the market list price using customer-specific, multi-dimension discount structures.
U13.trigger: Local price derivation for a customer with a discount structure.
flow: Select the customer's discount structure, for example competitive pressure against average price level.
Apply it off the market list price to derive the dealer price.
Support changing the structure's dimensions or their number.
Validate against minimum margin.
U13.inputs: Market list price, discount structure definition and dimensions.
U13.outputs: A dealer price per customer and customer type.
U13.pain: Discount structures maintained by hand drift quickly and obscure true net realisation.

U23.name: Customer-Price Calculation with Margin Check
U23.purpose: Calculate the final customer price off the dealer price, by structure or mark-up, with a minimum-margin check per entity.
U23.trigger: A customer price needs to be set off the derived dealer price.
flow: Apply the customer discount structure or a cost mark-up.
Run the minimum-margin check, differentiated per entity type.
Resolve any breach before storing.
Publish alongside the base price.
U23.inputs: Dealer price, customer structure or mark-up, minimum-margin thresholds.
U23.pain: Customer-price calculation without an enforced margin check is where late-stage leakage concentrates.

U14.name: Market Price Change
U14.purpose: Run a local price change through impact preview, approval and activation.
U14.trigger: A local repricing decision, cost pass-through, or competitive response.
flow: Define the change scope and proposed new prices.
Show the margin and revenue impact to the approver.
Route through the conditional approval workflow with tiered discount gates.
Activate on approval, separating communication and activation dates.
U14.inputs: Current local prices, cost and margin data, approval rules.
U14.outputs: An approved, activated local price change with rationale logged.
U14.pain: Approvers frequently decide without seeing the impact number, and approvals live in email rather than a tracked workflow.

U15.name: Simulate & Conduct a General Increase
U15.purpose: Simulate a general increase iteratively to reach a margin or revenue target, with suggested moves, then conduct it.
U15.trigger: A periodic general increase or a target-driven repricing.
flow: Change inputs such as exchange rate or drivers in simulation mode without implementing.
Calculate the effect on pricing KPIs.
Iterate to meet the target, and save and share named scenarios.
Promote the chosen scenario to an approved change.
U15.inputs: Current prices, target KPIs, driver and exchange-rate inputs.
U15.outputs: A saved, approved scenario aligned to the target.
U15.pain: Teams cannot test a general increase against targets before committing, so increases are blunt and miss the goal.

U16.name: Campaign & Promotion Pricing
U16.purpose: Run time-bound promotional prices with scoped validity, margin checks and automatic revert.
U16.trigger: A planned promotion, a slow-mover push, or a competitive campaign.
flow: Define the campaign scope, price and validity window.
Check minimum-margin and corridor compliance.
Route for approval and schedule activation.
Revert automatically at campaign end and measure uplift.
U16.inputs: Campaign scope, promotional price, margin floors, validity dates.
U16.outputs: A governed, time-boxed campaign price with measured effect.
U16.pain: Campaigns run outside the governed system tend to skip margin checks and never get their uplift measured.

U17.name: Special & Regional Price Requests
U17.purpose: Capture and maintain distributor, importer and key-account prices and regional requests with controlled eligibility.
U17.trigger: A negotiated agreement or a regional special-price request.
flow: Capture the request and its rationale from the region.
Apply the eligible price method and validate against floors.
Route through tiered approval gates.
Track validity and review on expiry.
U17.inputs: Request terms, eligibility rules, margin floors.
U17.outputs: An approved, time-bound special or regional price.
U17.pain: Special and regional prices proliferate without controlled eligibility and expiry, eroding net realisation.

U24.name: Agreements, Bonus & Long-Term Deals
U24.purpose: Manage commercial conditions (customer discounts, dealer bonuses, target agreements and long-term agreements) and simulate their scenarios.
U24.trigger: A new or renewing agreement, bonus scheme or long-term negotiation.
flow: Capture the commercial conditions: discounts, bonus, targets.
Store and process the contracts in the agreement module.
Simulate long-term-agreement scenarios against cost development and volume commitments.
Alert before supply obligations or contract end dates lapse.
U24.inputs: Contract terms, turnover thresholds, cost development, volume scenarios.
U24.outputs: Governed agreements with simulated scenarios and obligation alerts.
U24.pain: Agreements and long-term deals managed off-system hide their true margin effect and let obligations lapse unnoticed.

U25.name: Bid Monitoring & History
U25.purpose: Monitor the bidding process and inform new quotations with bid history.
U25.trigger: A new bid request or an in-flight bid to monitor.
flow: Capture the bid scope and required price points.
Check bid history for comparable past responses and outcomes.
Support the response within governance and margin floors.
Monitor the bid to decision.
U25.inputs: Bid scope, historical bid data, margin floors.
U25.pain: Without bid history, each quotation is built from scratch and repeats earlier pricing mistakes.

U18.name: Central Price Publication
U18.purpose: Publish approved central prices to the consuming ERP, logistics, product-information and invoicing systems with validated timing.
U18.trigger: Central prices are approved and due for activation.
flow: Package approved prices with their validity dates.
Publish to the consuming systems including product information.
Confirm receipt and consistency.
Separate approval, communication and activation dates.
U18.inputs: Approved central prices, validity dates, target-system interfaces.
U18.outputs: Published central prices confirmed in the consuming systems.
U18.pain: Publication without confirmation lets silent gaps reach invoicing and the customer.

U19.name: Market Price Distribution
U19.purpose: Distribute approved market prices flexibly to local consuming systems, channels and customer-specific formats.
U19.trigger: Local prices are approved and due for distribution.
flow: Select what to distribute: full or delta, range, future-dated.
Distribute via the right interface, in customer-specific formats.
Confirm receipt and synchronise validity dates centrally and locally.
Surface cross-market price differences for the same part.
U19.inputs: Approved local prices, channel interfaces, customer formats.
U19.outputs: Distributed local prices with synchronised validity.
U19.pain: Validity-date mismatch and manual reformatting per customer produce inconsistent live prices and wasted effort.

U20.name: Price Audit, History & Compliance
U20.purpose: Maintain a complete, retained audit trail and full traceability for every price change, with retention and deletion handling.
U20.trigger: Any price change, or a periodic audit or compliance review.
flow: Log who, what, when and why for every change under a unique reference.
Maintain traceability from the final price back to rule, driver, cost and approval.
Enforce retention, deletion and data-subject policies.
Generate compliance and price-health reports from the record.
U20.inputs: All pricing events, approval records, retention policy.
U20.outputs: A retained, queryable audit trail and compliance reports.
U20.pain: Audit demands (long retention, full traceability and deletion handling) recur everywhere yet are usually assembled manually.
